questions.question: Does the proxy look up a held or kept-blocked name before the person answers (DNS exfiltration, E-NET-07)?
questions.recommendation: No lookup leaves before an Allow at Full; the cell asserts zero lookups, and the local-address check runs after the Allow.

questions.question: Does an Allow-once host grant cover further requests on the same kept-alive connection (E-NET-18)?
questions.recommendation: One Allow once is one connection: requests on it ride it (the proxy decides by host and port and can't see them), and a new connection asks again.

questions.question: Q293 (no Allow next time on loopback) vs ADR 0067 qw384 (a loopback port of a service on this Mac is allowed by its one port): which wins for an unowned loopback port (E-NET-22, E-GRANT-03)?
questions.recommendation: qw384 keeps its port Allow for an unowned loopback port. Q293's no-Allow covers purlis's own ports, metadata, link-local and this machine's non-loopback addresses.

questions.question: At the chat's proxy, how is a host with userinfo, a trailing dot or punycode decided (E-NET-26)?
questions.recommendation: Userinfo is refused. A trailing dot is the same host and gets the same decision. Punycode is decided and shown in its ASCII form.

questions.question: After a host grant is removed, does an open CONNECT tunnel keep running (E-NET-27)?
questions.recommendation: Yes, as qw384b rules for port grants: it runs until it ends or the chat restarts, and new connections are decided again at once.

questions.question: At Basic, is Codex's provider-side `web_search` still disabled (E-NET-30)?
questions.recommendation: Yes, at every level, because it bypasses the proxy and the host record.

questions.question: Do refusals that only the kernel makes (UDP or netlink socket, signal, ptrace, setuid, userns, Apple Events, Launch Services, XPC) owe a block?
questions.recommendation: No block is owed where the OS reports nothing purlis receives. Where ticket 52's receiver sees one on macOS, it is a verified block (Q295). The cell asserts the escape failed and that nothing was seen.

questions.question: Is `vault-links.json` a class-1 vault store (E-FILE-19)?
questions.recommendation: Yes: it is unreadable at Full and Basic.

questions.question: Is reading `~/.ssh` private keys and the forge and cloud credential files denied? ADR 0067's floor says reads outside the denial classes aren't held, and Full doesn't say (E-FILE-20/21).
questions.recommendation: Deny the reads at Full and Basic, through an ADR 0067 amendment that names them as a class. Until then the cells follow the emitted deny list, and the person approves that list.

questions.question: macOS at Full and Basic: signalling other processes, direct XPC, the Keychain via `securityd`, the pasteboard (E-PROC-01, 06-08)?
questions.recommendation: Refused at both levels. The floor already holds the keychain's files, so `securityd` should match them.

questions.question: Do the floor's holds stated for Codex and OpenCode (Apple Events, Launch Services, launchd, unix sockets) apply to Claude Code's own sandbox on macOS?
questions.recommendation: Yes: expect refused. Ticket 10's leg proves it, and a gap is a p0 against the settings purlis compiles.

questions.question: At Basic, is a CONNECT to a host on a port its listing doesn't name carried (E-NET-13)?
questions.recommendation: Carried: the floor asks about no host or port.

questions.question: Is the listen grant (and so the door) offered at Basic as at Full (E-NET-20, E-DOOR-*)?
questions.recommendation: Yes, the same at both levels.

questions.question: At No sandbox the opt-out lifts class 3. Does purlisd still refuse human scopes to the chat's process tree, and is the seal key still app-only (E-SEC-04, E-PROC-07)?
questions.recommendation: Yes: the process-tree refusal and the Keychain's app-only access hold at every level.

questions.question: Is a hostile project harness config screened at No sandbox (E-FILE-28, E-FILE-33)?
questions.recommendation: No screening is owed at No sandbox. These rows are Full and Basic only.

questions.question: Does purlis end a chat's surviving children when the chat ends (E-PROC-02)?
questions.recommendation: Not owed: they stay confined. A later ticket can add the reaping.

questions.question: On Linux, may a wrapped chat create user namespaces (E-PROC-12)?
questions.recommendation: Refused by the seccomp filter, so a namespace can't remap round Landlock.

questions.question: What bound and what response apply to an oversized hook-socket line (E-IPC-04)?
questions.recommendation: Refused at the bound and the connection closed. Nothing is recorded as the chat, and the host keeps serving.

questions.question: `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` passes by design (ADR 0047), and purlis holds a per-chat agent (#1350, ADR 0067 2026-10-10-04 item 8). Is the socket it names reachable (E-IPC-08)?
questions.recommendation: purlis's per-chat agent is reachable by design. The person's own agent socket is unreachable unless granted.

questions.question: TIOCSTI and OSC 52 through the pane (E-IPC-12/13)?
questions.recommendation: TIOCSTI is refused by the Linux filter. purlis's pane drops OSC 52 writes to the pasteboard.
